as_written_in_papers.quote: The whole-exome sequencing (WES) (performed in Bioscientia Human Genetics) identified the heterozygous variant c.1420A>G (p.Thr474Ala) in exon7 of the TNFAIP3 gene (chr6:138200002), which leads to an amino acid exchange, and 10 of 16 bioinformatics in silico programs predict a pathogenic for this variant.

cases.statement: One person: a 12-year-old Saudi boy with chronic immune thrombocytopenia from age 9 and vitiligo, heterozygous by exome sequencing.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: chronic immune thrombocytopenia from age 9, resistant to steroids, rituximab and (later) eltrombopag; epistaxis and ecchymosis; vitiligo around the eyes and on the limbs; no oral or genital ulcers, no organomegaly or lymphadenopathy

quotes.quote: A 12-year-old-boy presented for the first time in April 2017.
He was diagnosed with ITP at the age of 9 years in a peripheral healthcare center.
He had multiple hospitalizations due to recurrent epistaxis and ecchymosis.
The dermatologist diagnosed it as vitiligo and prescribed topical tacrolimus.
There was no oral or genital ulceration, no organomegaly or lymphadenopathy, and his musculoskeletal system examination was normal.
This revealed heterozygous variant c.1420A>G (p.Thr474Ala) in exon7 of the TNFAIP3 gene (chr6:138200002).

phenotype_specificity.statement: The authors note the boy lacks the Behçet-like ulcers typical of the disease and say causation is unclear. Flow cytometry was used to rule out immunodeficiency and ALPS-type causes; no other genes are reported as tested or excluded beyond the exome.

quotes.quote: The features of the ulcers are consistent with Behcet’s syndrome. Our case did not report any such features.
Flow cytometry indicated the normal expression of HLA-ABC and HLA-DR on the lymphocytes, which ruled out immunodeficiency.
Taken together, it is unclear whether the detected heterozygous TNFAJP3 variant is causative for the phenotype of our patient.

segregation.statement: Not done (cost). Eight siblings and the non-consanguineous parents have no significant medical history; none were tested.

quotes.quote: The main limitation of this study is lack of segregation analysis test of the identified variant for parents and other family members to support WES finding.
He is a product of non-consanguineous parents, has eight siblings, none of whom have any significant medical history.
The test was not performed due to cost effectiveness.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense: c.1420A>G predicted p.(Thr474Ala). The paper states the disease arises from loss of function of TNFAIP3 (general statement, not about this variant).

quotes.quote: A loss of function mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene leads to haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20), which causes an auto-inflammatory condition [12].

computational_predictions.statement: 10 of 16 in-silico programs predicted a damaging effect, as reported (the programs are not named).

quotes.quote: which leads to an amino acid exchange, and 10 of 16 bioinformatics in silico programs predict a pathogenic for this variant.

population_data_in_papers.statement: The authors say the allele frequency in the general population has not been documented, and the variant was not in HGMD 2018.2.

quotes.quote: Allele frequency of this variant in the general population has not been documented, and this is the first time detected in The Human Gene Mutation Database.

authors_classification.statement: The authors classify it as a variant of uncertain significance.

quotes.quote: Considering the available information, the variant is classified as a variant of uncertain significance.

concerns: The paper names no transcript and gives the position as chr6:138200002 without an assembly; the batch VCF is GRCh38 6:137878865. The protein agrees (protein_check: agrees).
The phenotype (chronic ITP with vitiligo, no ulcers) is atypical for the disease as the paper itself describes it.
No segregation, parental testing or functional data.
notes_for_panel: Single case report; the evidence is the exome finding and an unnamed set of in-silico predictors (10 of 16). The authors themselves leave causation open.
